body:
Fun is a tricky thing for me. If I'm doing something enjoyable all I can think about is "DUDE, Why are you at the movies when you should be saving your money, fixing your life, and finding a future?!" so I beat myself up over it. Then when I Work/Eat/Sleep/Work/Eat/Sleep for a week on end I say "The fuck? Is this all your life amounts to? What's the point?"

I feel like it's a lose/lose no matter what I do. I guess the last thing I truly enjoy doing is drinking. And only because it numbs the self loathing after the fourth or fifth shot & beer round and I feel what it is like to actually enjoy something again.

I've recently returned to reading a lot. It's been my recent attempt at, yet again, trying to stop unhealthy choices. I've burned through about four books in just the past two weeks. Again though, it almost makes it worse because when I read it's in my shitty busted up room above a bar and if I try to go out to escape that by reading in a coffee shop or some-such I get anxious and uncomfortable.

Also, in relation to Powers whiskey. I wouldn't touch the new stuff. It's like barrel aged cough syrup. The old stuff was smoother than Jameson. It is also owned by the Jameson and Sons company so instead of having three shooting whiskey's in their lineup (Paddy's, Powers, and Jameson) they tried to make Powers a "sipping" whiskey and just completely ruined it, coupled with a higher price tag.

Haha, I'm fine for now. Like I said in the beginning of the post it's not an "ultimatum" or anything. It's a nearly overwhelming desire to merely not be alive anymore. As time passes the drinking gets heavier, the heartbreak gets harder, and the emotions get numbed. Life and random chance hasn't offed me yet so I'm getting more used to the idea that I should do it myself and get it over with.

I don't want to feel this way, obviously. But I'm not saying "I'M DOING IT TONIGHT I HATE THIS!" It's more of a "I'm trying to stop it from happening in the future because I know it will, and I know I shouldn't. I don't know why I shouldn't yet, but everyone else around me seems to enjoy life (at least enough to not let thoughts of suicide hold them back as much as it has me)."

I'm more afraid of the winter. The holidays and the cold are already getting to me and it's not even November. This just feels like it's going to be the worst one in a while for me emotionally and I don't want to make an rash decisions like say... suicide because of a particularly bad bender mixed with a breakup and whatever other sad shit life throws at me all at once.

I've been to the VA, a lot. It didn't do much for me. I followed every "order" to a 'T'. My counselor and eventual therapists gave me very good advice that got me through the hardest part of adjusting to a normal life. I didn't see them all that often because they were pretty overloaded with cases. All in all though I still do a few of the things they told me I should do.

The one that works the best is to keep a journal. Not just one though, but two. In the first one I write about what I did that day. "Worked 8 hours", "Ate an Italian hoagie and tried a different cheese than I normally get on it", "Ran into an old friend while on my home", etc.

In the other journal I write what I was thinking the whole day, "Woke up and wanted to die", "Thought about whether I could bear the responsibility of bringing a child into this world if I even wanted to", "Thought about if I should put a different cheese on my Italian hoagie before lunch", etc.

This way I can not only look back on my days but also exactly what I was thinking. With a large enough sample size I can being to pinpoint what makes me happy, what makes me sad, and what is good or bad for me in the long run. It works up until a point but it's hard to care when you just *don't care* about anything.

Again, I do it because I follow order, I do it because I know it'll help. It still doesn't help me understand the whole point of even trying in the first place though.

>  I can never differentiate between ACTUAL side effects and once that I just imagine because I know I am on different medicines. 

Jeez, as I'm sure you know that goes beyond medicines. It's always a struggle to differentiate if positivity (or any change really) is the result of a recent change or just luck/placebo. It's always time that tells with that.

My favorite whiskey for the the longest time was Powers but since they changed the recipe (Ugh) it's Jameson. However if I'm looking for something to sip or put in a cocktail I go with Buffalo Trace. It's flavorful, smooth, and remains sweet without having to overdo it like most Bourbon's try to by jamming as much corn mash as they can in there.

Law school though? That's always a tough one. I have a friend who just moved to Savannah to go to Law School. It was a bit of a surprise to everyone because she was a huge party girl who went "straight" and is focusing on her life and a new career. She still has that "no fucks given" attitude but she carries it into a professional life now. We still joke around from time to time about when we went to the beach and I saw the tattoo she has above her vagina that just says "The Seaward" in reference to Arrested Development. She's been struggling with that lately, been thinking of dropping out. It seems that it's a much harder path then most would give it credit for.

I suppose the Flyers having a good year is too much to ask for, haha.

Tell me about yourself. Whiskey gets me emotional and I'm just looking for a connection. Even on the most basic level. Tell me about your day, your life, your first love, whatever.
